engine.title: The multibagger screen qualified nobody for four weeks
engine.body: Corrects what this entry said on 2026-08-27. It read ‘the scan is running on schedule’ and blamed the fixed list on cadence. The ledger says otherwise: the last multibagger row is 2026-08-01, while magic, magicmagic and ai_longterm — the same Saturday job, the same slot — all logged 2026-08-22. Twenty-six days, three Saturdays, nothing written.
engine.note: The screen is not broken. Run on 2026-08-27 it took 11 candidates and rejected 10 for R:R below 2.0 — CHENNPETRO 1.29, FLUOROCHEM 1.07, GLAXO 0.59, which needs a 63% win rate merely to break even. The defect was that a week qualifying nobody wrote nothing at all, so the page served the 1 August list as though it were current. The attempt is recorded either way now. The gate is NOT loosened: publishing a 0.59 R:R to keep the section busy is the exact trade this screen exists to refuse, and an empty week is a real result.

engine.title: Stop buying strength that has already run
engine.body: The 4H RSI ceiling for longs was 75. Splitting every closed trade by the RSI recorded at entry showed the engine bleeding above 65 and profitable below it. The ceiling is now 65.
engine.note: Holds in both halves of the sample and at every cut point tested (60, 65, 70), so it is not one lucky threshold. The threshold was still chosen from this sample, so treat the size as an upper bound.

engine.title: A break-even stop would not have helped
engine.body: The median losing trade was +1.44R in profit before it reversed, and 59% touched a full +1R first. That looks like an obvious fix: move the stop to entry once price pays 1R. Re-walking every trade bar by bar, with winners subject to the same rule, says otherwise.
engine.note: The first version of this test only altered losers, which guarantees a positive answer. Correcting it reversed the conclusion. Nothing tested cleared one standard error, so no stop rule was adopted.

engine.title: Trades were being closed at prices that never traded
engine.body: The grader had never resolved a single trade — an exception was being swallowed silently — leaving a fallback path that could book an exit at a bar from before the signal existed. Every closed trade was re-graded against bars that actually printed.
evidence: exits corrected to a real price
engine.note: This moved the headline number against me. It is published anyway, because the earlier number was not real. Pre-correction data is kept in the repo rather than deleted.

engine.title: A first target must pay back the risk
engine.body: T1 was whichever structural level sat nearest the entry, with no distance test. One signal shipped a T1 worth 0.19R against its own stop, printed beside an R:R of 2.41 quoted off T2. T1 must now return at least 1R.

chess.title: Strategy: Pawn Structure
chess.body: Your pawn structure dictates your plan. Doubled pawns (two pawns on same file) = weakness. Isolated pawn = can't be defended by a pawn, needs piece protection. Passed pawn = no enemy pawn can stop it = future queen. Backward pawn = can't advance, target for opponent. Know your pawn structure and play accordingly.

wisdom.title: The Long Game of Parenting
wisdom.body: You won't remember 2026 as a year. You'll remember it as the year your daughter started talking, your first steps in Dubai, the grind that changed everything. Keep a journal. Even one line per day. In 10 years, you'll read it and understand why it was worth it.

book.author: Stephen Covey
book.lesson: 10% of life is what happens to you. 90% is how you respond. This is the core of proactivity: between stimulus and response, there is a gap. In that gap is your freedom to choose. Reactive people let their moods and circumstances determine their behaviour. Proactive people subordinate impulse to values. Covey's Circle of Influence vs Circle of Concern: proactive people focus on what they can control (Circle of Influence) and it expands. Reactive people focus on what they cannot control (Circle of Concern) — market conditions, other people's behaviour, the economy — and feel increasingly helpless.
book.key_quote: Focus on what you can control. Your response is always within your Circle of Influence.
book.action: List 3 things worrying you. Categorise each: can I influence this or not? Only spend energy on the ones you can influence.
crux: Character ethic beats personality ethic. Techniques without character are manipulation.
Paradigms determine what you see. Change the map before optimising the route.
Habit 1 — Be Proactive: between stimulus and response is your freedom to choose.
Focus on your Circle of Influence, not your Circle of Concern. The first grows; the second drains.
Habit 2 — Begin with the End in Mind: write the personal mission statement, then live backwards from it.
Habit 3 — First Things First: Quadrant II (important, not urgent) is where effectiveness lives.
Urgency addiction disguises itself as productivity. Most of Quadrant I is neglected Quadrant II.
Habit 4 — Think Win/Win: scarcity thinking produces win/lose; abundance produces cooperation.
Habit 5 — Seek First to Understand, Then to Be Understood. Diagnose before prescribing.
Empathic listening is the highest-leverage communication skill and almost nobody does it.
Habit 6 — Synergise: 1+1 can equal 3 when differences are valued rather than tolerated.
Habit 7 — Sharpen the Saw: renew physical, mental, social/emotional, spiritual capacity.
P/PC balance: production versus production capability. Killing the goose for the eggs.
The Emotional Bank Account — trust accumulates through deposits and is spent by withdrawals.
learnings: Effectiveness is a private victory before it is a public one.
Quadrant II work never announces itself. You must schedule it.
Most communication failures are prescription before diagnosis.
Renewal is not a reward for finishing. It is the capacity to finish.
examples: Viktor Frankl in the camps: everything removed except the choice of response. The origin of Habit 1.
Covey's funeral exercise — what four speakers would say about you — reframes goals from achievement to character.
The father who lists his son's faults and cannot understand why the son won't talk. Diagnosis skipped entirely.
adapt: Circle of influence on the Meta case: control the caption process, not the platform's decision.
Quadrant II: the Dubai applications and the daughter's bedtime. Neither is urgent. Both decide the decade.
Sharpen the saw is not optional at 7 hours' sleep — it is what makes the analysis correct.
Emotional bank account at home: presence deposits daily. The balance is what carries the hard months.

minimalism.title: Digital Minimalism First
minimalism.body: Physical clutter is visible and therefore self-limiting. Digital clutter is infinite. 40,000 unread emails and 200 apps cost more attention than a messy room ever did.
minimalism.action: Delete every app you have not opened in 30 days. No exceptions for 'might need'.
minimalism.label: Minimalism

etiquette.title: Introduce People Properly
etiquette.body: Do not just exchange names — give each person a reason to care. 'Sara, this is Ahmed, he rebuilt their close process in six weeks.' You have just made both look good.
etiquette.action: Make one introduction today with a reason attached.
etiquette.label: Etiquette

stillness.title: The Sabbath Principle
stillness.body: One day in seven with no optimisation, no side project, no market. Every durable tradition independently arrived at this. They were not being inefficient.
stillness.action: Block one screen-free half-day this week. Defend it.
stillness.label: Stillness

model.title: Skin In The Game
model.body: Discount any forecast from someone who bears no cost for being wrong. Advice without exposure is entertainment, however credentialed the source.

drill.body: A single number is a guess dressed up. Run it at -20%, base, and +20% and present the range. Nobody credible presents one number.

father.title: Stop at eye contact
father.do: When she catches your eye across the room, stop and respond — smile, wave, say her name.
father.why: Social referencing is beginning: she checks your face to decide how to feel about things. Responding consistently makes you a reliable reference point.

father.title: Let her lead the play
father.do: Follow what she reaches for instead of redirecting to the toy you chose. Sit on the floor at her level for 15 minutes.
father.why: Serve-and-return interaction builds the circuitry for attention and self-regulation. Following her focus teaches that her signals produce a response — the root of secure attachment.

life_wisdom.teaching: Jain metaphysics treats karma as fine matter that adheres to the soul through action and intent. Unusually, intent matters as much as the act.
life_wisdom.apply: Judge your own decisions on intent and process, not only outcome. A profitable trade taken for bad reasons still deposits the bad habit.

life_wisdom.teaching: In the traditional sequence of practices, generosity comes before ethics and meditation — as the foundation rather than the reward.
life_wisdom.apply: Give something away before you feel you have surplus. Time or attention counts; the point is that it precedes abundance rather than following it.

speaking.title: Handle 'I do not know'
speaking.drill: Rehearse: 'I do not have that number in front of me. I will have it to you by Thursday.' Say it without apology.
speaking.why: Senior people say this comfortably. Guessing to avoid it is how credibility is actually lost.

interview_tech.q: What is your WACC and how would you set the hurdle rate for a new store?
interview_tech.a: WACC = cost of equity × equity weight + after-tax cost of debt × debt weight. Cost of equity via CAPM: risk-free rate plus beta times equity risk premium, with a country risk premium for emerging markets. But do not use group WACC as the store hurdle — a new store in a new market is riskier than the average of the existing business. Add a premium and be explicit about it. The common error is a single group hurdle applied to everything, which systematically over-invests in risky projects and under-invests in safe ones.

interview_tech.q: Your ERP implementation is running three months late. What do you tell the steering committee?
interview_tech.a: The date, the cause, the options with costs, and your recommendation. Be specific about which workstream is late and why — usually data migration or the volume of unresolved customisation requests, not the software. Present the real choice: go live late and clean, or on time with manual workarounds and a defined remediation plan. Quantify the workaround cost in FTE months. Having led D365 across two countries, the credible line is that data quality determines the date more than configuration does.

interview_soft.q: How do you stay current technically while managing?
interview_soft.a: Be specific and verifiable. Name the standard you last read in full and why, the technical update you attended, the thing you built yourself recently rather than delegated. Vague answers about 'reading widely' land badly with technical interviewers. The strongest version connects it to a decision: 'I went back through IFRS 16 properly when we hit the lease modification question on the Indonesian stores, and that changed how we structured the renewal.'

interview_soft.q: Where do you think retail is heading in the next five years?
interview_soft.a: Have a view and defend it with numbers, not trends. Something like: physical stores stop being judged on their own sales as fulfilment and returns blur the channels, which breaks conventional store P&L and forces a catchment-level view; margin pressure shifts from price to cost-to-serve; and in the Gulf specifically, corporate tax and e-invoicing professionalise finance functions that were previously light. Then say what you would do about it in the role you are interviewing for.

cfo_field.q: Explain a variance in one sentence or you do not understand it yet.
cfo_field.a: 'Margin is down 180bps: 120 from promotional depth in electronics, 40 from freight, 20 mix.' That is a CFO answer. A table of forty lines is a controller answer. The discipline is to decompose until the drivers are additive and then name the largest two. If you cannot make the bridge add up, you have a data problem, not a communication problem.

cfo_field.q: Working capital is where a retail CFO is actually judged.
cfo_field.a: EBITDA gets the headline; the cash conversion cycle gets the board's attention. DIO + DSO − DPO. Retail is inventory-heavy and often near-zero DSO, so the fight is DIO against DPO. Cutting DIO from 95 to 80 days on AED 400M COGS releases roughly AED 16.4M of cash — permanently, without selling a single extra unit. That is a bigger number than most cost programmes deliver, and it does not need a headcount conversation.

lichess_games.analysis: Focus on early king safety: after 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 d6, develop knights before pushing ...f5; avoid premature pawn storms that expose your king.

lichess_summary.session_summary: AKK_010’s lone loss came from a sloppy opening choice that left the king exposed and the central pawn structure fragmented—avoid any gambit lines that sacrifice central control before you’ve mastered basic development. Focus on mastering the classical e4‑e5 or d4‑d5 setups, ensuring you complete the first three moves (develop knights, secure the center, castle) before launching any attacks. Drill the fundamental endgame motifs (king‑pawn opposition, basic rook lifts) for 30 minutes daily; until you can convert a simple material advantage, no aggressive repertoire will save you from repeat defeats.
